cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative ring R, ideal I and subset T of Spec R, T⊆V(I) if and only if I is contained in the ideal of elements vanishing on all primes in T.
cards.proof_strategy: Expand vanishing as membership in each prime ideal in T.
sketch_steps: Fix I and T.
Expand vanishing as membership in each prime ideal in T.
Both containments assert that each element of I lies in each prime of T.
Reorder the universal quantifiers to obtain the equivalence.

cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative ring R and subset T of Spec R, V of the vanishing ideal of T is exactly the Zariski closure of T.
cards.proof_strategy: Closed sets of Spec R are zero loci.
sketch_steps: Fix an arbitrary subset T, not necessarily closed.
Closed sets of Spec R are zero loci.
The vanishing ideal determines the smallest zero locus containing T.
This smallest closed superset is the closure of T.

cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative ring R and ideal I, the ideal vanishing on V(I) is the radical of I.
cards.proof_strategy: Every prime containing I contains its radical.
sketch_steps: Take the intersection of all primes containing I.
Every prime containing I contains its radical.
Prime ideal separation detects any element outside the radical.
The intersection is therefore exactly the radical.

cards.proof_strategy: Replace any set of equations by the ideal it generates.

The zero locus is unchanged by taking this generated ideal.
Conversely every ideal zero locus is closed.

cards.proof_strategy: The vanishing ideal of a singleton point is that prime ideal.
sketch_steps: View the point p as its underlying prime ideal.
The vanishing ideal of a singleton point is that prime ideal.
The general closure formula applies to the singleton.
Thus its specializations are exactly the primes containing p.

cards.canonical_statement: A point of Spec R is closed if and only if its underlying prime ideal is maximal.
cards.proof_strategy: A maximal ideal has no strictly larger prime ideal.
sketch_steps: The closure of a prime point is the set of primes above it.
A maximal ideal has no strictly larger prime ideal.

cards.proof_strategy: The quotient contraction map is therefore surjective as well as injective.
sketch_steps: Every prime ideal contains I by the nilradical assumption.

Surjectivity of the ring quotient makes this map a closed embedding.
A bijective closed embedding is a homeomorphism.

cards.canonical_statement: For any surjective ring homomorphism R→S, the Krull dimension of S is at most the Krull dimension of R, including infinite dimensions and the zero ring convention.
cards.proof_strategy: Surjectivity ensures distinct primes have distinct contractions.
sketch_steps: Contract a strict chain of prime ideals in S to R.
Surjectivity ensures distinct primes have distinct contractions.
Thus contraction preserves strictness and chain length.
Taking the supremum of all chain lengths gives the dimension inequality.

cards.canonical_statement: For any commutative Noetherian ring R, dim R[X]=dim R+1, with dimension taken in WithBot ℕ∞ so that zero and infinite-dimensional cases use the same formula.
cards.proof_strategy: Prime-chain arguments give the lower bound from adjoining one indeterminate.
sketch_steps: Retain the Noetherian hypothesis on R.
Prime-chain arguments give the lower bound from adjoining one indeterminate.
The Noetherian height theorem supplies the matching upper bound.
The two bounds establish equality in the extended dimension order.

cards.canonical_statement: For every prime ideal p of a commutative ring R, the Krull dimension of the local ring R_p equals the height of p, allowing infinite height.
cards.proof_strategy: This correspondence preserves and reflects strict chains.
sketch_steps: The prime ideals of R_p correspond to primes of R contained in p.
This correspondence preserves and reflects strict chains.
The maximal ideal of R_p corresponds to p itself.
The supremum of the chain lengths is both dim R_p and the height of p.
